title: Zerodha's Nithin Kamath to Startups: Stop Saying 'We Use AI'
excerpt: India's biggest online brokerage founder says AI marketing has become meaningless, arguing startups should focus on real product differentiation instead of hollow tech labels.
body:
• Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath has called out startups for making "we use AI" a selling point, arguing it has become meaningless marketing
  • Kamath has consistently questioned AI hype since 2021, when Zerodha's CTO called "powered by AI" claims "superfluous marketing, pure hogwash"
  • Despite skepticism about AI marketing, Kamath acknowledges AI will reshape financial services and has implemented an internal AI policy at Zerodha

Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath has a blunt message for India's startup ecosystem: stop bragging about using AI.

In a post that has sparked debate across India's tech and startup circles, Kamath argued that touting AI as a product feature has become a hollow marketing tactic. Bragging that your product uses AI is no longer a differentiator, Kamath said — it is table stakes at best, and misleading at worst.

A Consistent AI Skeptic

The comments are the latest in a years-long pattern of AI skepticism from India's largest online brokerage founder. Back in 2021, when AI marketing was reaching fever pitch across India's fintech sector, Kamath shared a note from Zerodha's CTO Kailash Nadh that dismissed most AI claims in the industry.

https://x.com/MoneycontrolH/status/2088884113235427381

"From my interactions with the industry, I am strongly inclined to say that most of the claims of being 'powered by AI' is superfluous marketing, pure hogwash."

— Kailash Nadh, CTO, Zerodha

At the time, Kamath himself said he had not found any use case for AI or ML at Zerodha, despite repeatedly being asked how the company used the technology. SEBI's quarterly surveys of AI and ML usage across brokerages backed up the claim — most reported no meaningful deployment.

From Skeptic to Pragmatist

Kamath's stance has evolved since then, though not in the direction AI boosters might hope. By 2023, he acknowledged that breakthroughs in generative AI would "take away jobs and can disrupt society," and Zerodha created an internal AI policy pledging not to fire employees whose roles were made redundant by technology.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=eZdrpChV0C4

Earlier this year, he argued that AI can make investors "more disciplined, but not smarter" and that it cannot generate alpha in markets as long as human biases remain in the loop.

"As long as there's a human in the loop, you're still dealing with the same creature driven by fear and greed, and that human will keep making the same mistakes."

— Nithin Kamath, CEO, Zerodha

The Real Competitive Moats

Kamath has consistently argued that trust, infrastructure, and genuine product focus matter far more than AI labels. Zerodha reached 1.1 crore customers without ever running advertisements and operates with roughly 1,000 employees — a deliberate choice to stay lean while investing in partner startups like Smallcase, Sensibull, and Ditto.

Looking ahead, Kamath envisions a future where AI-powered apps will handle investing, trading, banking, and payments, with brokers reduced to "pipes connecting users to exchanges and back-office systems." In that world, he has said, "trust and infrastructure will be our only real moats."

Why It Matters for Indian Startups

Kamath's intervention comes as India's startup ecosystem remains awash in AI-first pitches. With funding rounds increasingly tied to AI narratives, the pressure to slap an AI label on products — regardless of whether the technology is meaningful to the core offering — has intensified across sectors from fintech to edtech to healthtech.

The message from India's most successful bootstrapped startup founder is pointed: AI is a tool, not a strategy. If your main selling point is that you use it, you probably have not built anything worth talking about.
